title: Library Management
summary: Design a library system for members to search, borrow, reserve and return books, with fines for late returns.
description:
A public library wants to replace its paper records.

The library owns many **physical copies** of each **book title**. **Members** can search the catalogue, **borrow** available copies, **reserve** titles that are all checked out, and **return** them. Late returns incur a **fine**. Librarians add books and manage members. When a reserved title comes back, the waiting member is **notified**.

Focus on the difference between a *book* and a *copy*, on who enforces the borrowing rules, and on how notifications and fines can evolve.

functionalRequirements.text: The catalogue stores book titles (ISBN, title, authors) and their physical copies.
Members can search the catalogue by title, author or subject.
A member can borrow up to 5 copies at a time, each for 14 days.
A member can reserve a title when no copy is available; reservations are served first-come-first-served.
Returning a copy late creates a fine; members with unpaid fines cannot borrow.
When a reserved title is returned, the next member in the queue is notified.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Borrowing rules (limits, loan period) differ for student and faculty members and may change.
New notification channels (SMS, push) can be added without changing lending code.

variationPoints.name: Borrowing policy
variationPoints.description: Limits and loan periods differ by member type and change over time.

variationPoints.name: Notification channel
variationPoints.description: Email today; SMS and push later.

extensionScenario.prompt: The library adds e-books with unlimited simultaneous loans but a 7-day licence, plus SMS notifications. What changes in your model?

hints.title: Book vs copy
hints.text: A Book is the title (ISBN, authors). A BookCopy is the physical thing on a shelf with a barcode and status. Loans reference copies; reservations reference books.

hints.title: Who enforces the rules?
hints.text: Avoid putting borrowing limits inside Member. A LendingService (or Library) asks a BorrowingPolicy for the rules of this member type, so faculty/student rules can change independently.

hints.title: Decouple notifications
hints.text: When a copy is returned, publish an event. A ReservationQueue/NotificationService subscribes and notifies through a NotificationChannel interface (Email, SMS).

curveballs.title: E-books and SMS
curveballs.prompt: The library adds e-books with unlimited simultaneous loans but a 7-day licence, plus SMS notifications. What changes in your model?

curveballs.title: Premium members
curveballs.prompt: A paid Premium membership borrows 10 copies for 28 days and pays half fines. Students keep today's rules.

curveballs.title: Grace period and fine cap
curveballs.prompt: Fines now start after a 2-day grace period and are capped at the book's replacement price.
